back: Google's time-series foundation model: a decoder-only transformer on patches, pretrained on a large mix of real and synthetic series, used zero-shot.
They cut the number of tokens. Attention cost grows with tokens squared, so patches are cheaper and allow a longer context.
Chronos (Amazon), TimesFM (Google), Moirai (Salesforce), Lag-Llama, and TimeGPT (Nixtla).

front: Five questions to judge a foundation-model claim?
back: Which baselines, which metric, which split and leakage, what cost, and are covariates used?

front: How should you use a foundation model first?
back: As a zero-shot baseline and ensemble member, compared with seasonal naive, ETS and a tuned GBM on a rolling backtest.

front: A common limit of zero-shot models?
back: Many use only the target history, so they cannot use known future information such as price or promotions.
